text:
Faster Payment, add payee. Before a new payee is saved, the bank checks the name the customer typed against the name on the receiving account. The customer must
  see the result before they can continue, understand what it means for their money, and choose whether to edit the details, carry on, or cancel. Make clear that
  the bank may not be able to recover a payment sent to the wrong account. Mobile first.

args.why: Seq 7 requires the customer to resolve a non-match Confirmation of Payee result unaided, seq 23 scopes close-match/no-match as in-bounds and forbids skipping the check or blocking payment after no-match, and seq 8 requires the irrevocability warning before the customer commits — this screen shows the name-check result and makes the decision (edit, continue, or cancel via back) explicit before the payee is saved.

text:
Proposed **confirm-payee-name-check**: a `screen-header` (back = cancel this step), a `card` holding one `list-row` that surfaces the Confirmation of Payee result (name entered vs. name on the account, with status/tone), and an inline `modal-dialog` carrying the irrevocability warning with `confirmLabel: "Continue anyway"` / `dismissLabel: "Edit payee details"`.

Rationale: seq 7 requires the customer to resolve a non-match result alone, with no agent to explain it; seq 23 scopes close-match and no-match as in-bounds and explicitly forbids letting a customer skip the check or be blocked after a no-match; seq 8 requires the Faster Payments irrevocability warning to surface before commitment. The three-way choice the brief asks for (edit / carry on / cancel) is expressed without inventing a third button: `modal-dialog`'s two paths give edit-or-continue, and the screen's own back action gives cancel — keeping the screen inside the `confirm` template (`screen-header`, `card?`, `modal-dialog`) rather than adding a `primary-button`/`ghost-button` pair the template doesn't name.

Added `close-match` and `no-match` as explicit extra states beyond the five-state floor, since seq 23 names both outcomes by name. Flagging one gap against the vocabulary: `list-row.tone` only runs `neutral|warn|critical`, so a true "no match" (critical) and "close match" (warn) are distinguishable, but there's no dedicated "match"-badge part — the result is read off `list-row.status`'s free text rather than a typed enum, which the owner may want to note if a stricter chip is wanted later.

text:
Add payee screen with Confirmation of Payee. The customer enters payee name, sort code and account number, then the bank checks the name against the account
  holder. Declare four states: match (continue), close match (show the real account name and offer to use it), no match (warn clearly, allow edit or proceed at
  own risk), unavailable (check could not run, explain and allow proceed or cancel). State that wrong-account payments may not be recoverable. Mobile.

text:
Proposed **add-payee-cop-check**, replacing the earlier account-number-only version now that the brief specifies the full entry-plus-check flow:

- `screen-header` ("Add a payee", back enabled)
- Three `text-field`s for payee name, sort code, account number — the minimum the check needs
- A persistent `text` caption stating the irrecoverability risk (seq 8), shown in every state, not just the failure ones, since it's a standing fact rather than a per-state report
- One `modal-dialog`, hidden by default, carrying the decision surface shared by the three conditional states:
  - **close-match** → body reveals the real account-holder name, `confirmLabel: "Use this name"` / `dismissLabel: "Keep what I typed"` (props swap per state)
  - **no-match** → body warns plainly, `confirmLabel: "Continue anyway"` / `dismissLabel: "Edit payee details"`
  - **unavailable** → body explains the check couldn't run, `confirmLabel: "Proceed anyway"` / `dismissLabel: "Cancel"`
  - **match** maps to the floor's `ideal` state: no modal, `primary-button` just continues
- `primary-button` ("Continue") last, as the one committing action

Declared `close-match`, `no-match`, `unavailable` as the extra states beyond the five-state floor, since the brief names them explicitly; `match` is covered by the existing `ideal` state rather than duplicated.

One tension worth flagging: the `modal-dialog` is a single part whose title/body/confirmLabel/dismissLabel must be rewritten per state to carry three different decisions (use-real-name, edit-or-proceed, proceed-or-cancel) — faithful to "a state sets props, never adds a part," but it means the three decisions share one visual shape rather than three differently-worded dialogs existing side by side. Also, `list-row`/`status-chip` were considered for depicting the match result itself but didn't fit either part's enum vocabulary (`status-chip.value` is `ok|due|overdue`, not match terminology), so the result reads through the modal's own body copy rather than a dedicated status part.

Proposed **payee-name-check-result** as its own screen, separate from `add-payee` — it reads the outcome only, no entry fields:

- `screen-header` ("Payee name check", back enabled)
- `card` → single `list-row` showing the account's real name against what was typed, with `status`/`tone` carrying the result (`Match` neutral by default; state props swap in "Close match"/"No match"/"Check unavailable" with `warn`/`critical` tone)
- A standing `text` caption with the irrecoverability warning (seq 8) — visible in every state, not just the failing ones, since it's a constant fact, not a per-state report
- `modal-dialog`, hidden in the match/ideal state, carrying the three decisions:
  - **close-match** → body shows the real name, `confirmLabel: "Use this name"` / `dismissLabel: "Keep what I entered"`
  - **no-match** → body warns plainly, `confirmLabel: "Continue anyway"` / `dismissLabel: "Edit payee details"`
  - **unavailable** → body explains the check didn't run, `confirmLabel: "Continue anyway"` / `dismissLabel: "Cancel"`
- `primary-button` ("Continue") last, for the **match** case — mapped to the floor's `ideal` state, where there's nothing to decide and the person just proceeds

Declared `close-match`, `no-match`, `unavailable` as the named extra states; `match` needs no extra entry since it's the ideal state.

One deliberate departure to flag: the `confirm` template's part list is `screen-header, card?, modal-dialog` with no `primary-button`. I added `primary-button` anyway, because three of the four states are genuine decisions (modal-dialog) but the fourth — a clean match — is not a decision at all, just a result to acknowledge and a path to continue; the general rule that every screen's one committing action is a trailing full-width `primary-button` seemed to govern that path, over the template's narrower list. Worth the owner's explicit call on whether that reading is right, or whether a clean match should also route through the modal's `confirmLabel` instead, keeping the screen strictly to the template.

text:
Scam-safety stop, after the payee name check and before send. Before a first payment to a new payee, pause the customer and ask about common scam signs: someone
  told them to move money, someone claiming to be the bank or police, pressure to act fast. They can cancel or continue. Keep the warning that a wrong payment
  may not be recoverable. Don't repeat the payee entry fields or the name check result.

This turn forks on seq 8 — the riskiest assumption is whether a screen, with no agent's ear, can do the scam-catching job the phone used to do. The PRD leaves open *how* the screen should attempt that: by collecting explicit self-report signals, or by forcing a uniform warning everyone must read and clear regardless of what they'd say. I'm proposing both as the same screen under two different answers.

args.why: Answers seq 8's open riskiest-assumption by betting that a screen can approximate the agent's ear through self-reported signal: explicit checkbox questions mirror what the agent used to ask aloud (told to move money, bank/police impersonation, pressure to act fast), and only a flagged answer escalates to the irrecoverability warning and the cancel-or-continue choice — unflagged customers pass through with minimal friction, keeping seq 7's no-call completion intact.

text:
Filed both options of **scam-safety-stop** against seq 8's open assumption:

**Option A (seq 36) — self-report checklist.** Three `choice` checkboxes mirror the agent's own questions (told to pay, bank/police impersonation, pressure to act fast). Unflagged answers pass through to `primary-button`; any flagged box escalates to `decision-modal` with the irrecoverability warning and the cancel-or-continue choice. Bets that explicit self-report is a workable proxy for the agent's ear, and keeps friction low for the unflagged majority — in keeping with seq 7's no-call completion goal.

**Option B (seq 37) — universal warning gate.** No checkboxes at all — every customer meets the same `decision-modal`, which states the same three scam signs as plain warning copy, before the cancel-or-continue choice. Bets that self-report can't be trusted (a coached customer may answer falsely), so the screen's only move is uniform friction rather than selective signal-collection.

Both keep the brief's constraints: no repeated payee fields or name-check result, the irrecoverability warning present, and cancel-or-continue as the only two paths through — differing only in whether the screen tries to *ask* anything before it warns. The owner's pick is itself evidence toward or against seq 8's riskiest assumption, which is exactly what the open fork calls for.

intro.content: We couldn't load this check. Try again before you continue.

args.why: Seq 14 ties Meridian's reimbursement defence to being able to show what the customer was shown and when, so a load failure on this mandatory warning can't quietly fall back to letting the payment through \u2014 the dialog stays hidden since it isn't trustworthy to show broken, and the one action is to retry, never a silent continue; seq 7 keeps that retry inline so the customer isn't pushed to call.

text:
Proposed the **error** state of `scam-safety-stop` (f11):

- `intro` reports the fault plainly: "We couldn't load this check. Try again before you continue." — reason before action, per the copy rules
- `recovery-notice` stays visible — it's a standing fact independent of whether the check loaded
- `decision-modal` hidden — if the warning content itself failed to render, showing it half-broken would be worse than not showing it, and critically there's no legitimate "continue anyway" path here: this gate is the thing standing between the customer and an irreversible payment
- `continue-button` relabelled "Try again" — deliberately *not* "Continue anyway"; a technical failure to load the mandatory scam warning can't become a silent bypass of it

The key design choice here: unlike a typical error state that just needs a retry path, this one carries extra weight from seq 14 — Meridian's APP-scam reimbursement defence depends on being able to show what the customer was shown and when. If the warning didn't load, there's no evidence it was shown, so the only honest move is retry, never skip-through.

text:
Send screen, the final step after the scam-safety stop. Shows the payee name, the amount and a Send button; don't repeat the entry fields, name check or scam
  questions. Declare three states: pending (payment in progress, may be held for checks, don't send again), success (sent, with a payment reference and time) and
  fail (didn't go, no money taken, what to do next). Each state must say clearly whether the money has left the account.

args.why: The final step after the scam-safety stop (seq 8's gate) and seq 7's no-call completion requirement: shows only payee and amount, commits with one Send action, and each of the three named states states plainly whether money has left the account, which matters directly to seq 14's point that Meridian's accountability and evidence obligations hinge on what happened and when.

text:
Proposed **send-payment**, the final step after `scam-safety-stop`:

- `screen-header` ("Send payment", back enabled)
- `list` → `list-row`s for Payee and Amount (the only entry data repeated, as a read-only summary, not fields), plus `reference-row` and `time-row` left empty in the base/ideal state and filled only on success — so the base screen already carries every part the success state needs, per the state rule that a state can set props but never add a part
- `money-status` text — a dedicated line whose wording changes per state to always say clearly whether money has left the account, as the brief requires:
  - ideal: "No money has left your account yet."
  - **pending**: money-status → "Your payment is being processed and may be held for checks. No money has left your account yet — don't send it again." `send-button` disabled, reference/time rows stay empty
  - **success**: money-status → "£250.00 has left your account." `reference-row`/`time-row` filled in, `send-button` disabled or relabelled (no further action needed)
  - **fail**: money-status → "This payment didn't go through. No money has left your account." `send-button` relabelled "Try again"
- `primary-button` ("Send payment") last, the one committing action

Declared `pending`, `success`, `fail` as the extra states beyond the five-state floor, using the brief's own names rather than mapping them silently onto loading/ideal/error, since the brief treats them as the screen's specific vocabulary.

One gap to flag: the vocabulary has no dedicated "amount" or "currency" part — `list-row.value` is a free string, so "£250.00" is carried as plain text rather than through any amount-typed part, and there's no `status-chip`-like part whose enum matches pending/success/fail, so the money-left-or-not fact rests entirely on the `money-status` text line rather than a typed status part.
